title: Certificate Holdings and the Way the Personal Checking Closing Charge Is Taken
content:
Once the level of the closing charge on a Personal Checking account has been set, two cases change the way it is taken, both read from the owner's certificate principal held under Certificates of Deposit, from how long the account has been open, and from the owner's card payments under Personal Credit Cards.

**First case.** Where the owner's certificate principal reaches the certificate relationship minimum of 25000.00 and the account has been open at least as long as the settled account period of 60 days, the closing charge is spread evenly over the whole months the account has been open, a month counting only once the day of the month the account was opened has come round again and the count never falling below one, and the result rounded half-up to the cent.

**Second case.** Where the case above does not apply and either the owner holds any certificate principal at all or the owner has made at least 15 card payments in the last twelve months, the closing charge is taken at half the level it was set, rounded half-up to the cent.

**Otherwise.** Where neither case applies, the charge is not taken in either of those ways.

**Worked treatments on hypothetical inputs.** With the level set at 24.00:

| Owner's position | Whole months open | Closing charge taken |
|---|---|---|
| Certificate principal of 30000.00, account opened on the 9th and handled five months later on the 20th | 5 | 4.80 |
| Certificate principal of 30000.00, account opened on the 9th and handled two months later on the 3rd | 1, the opening day of the month not having come round a second time | 24.00 |
| Certificate principal of 30000.00, account open 20 days | Not reached; the first case needs 60 days | 12.00, the any-principal limb of the second case being met |
| Certificate principal of 700.00, account open 400 days |  | 12.00 |
| No certificate principal, 16 card payments in the last twelve months |  | 12.00 |
| No certificate principal, 2 card payments |  | Neither case applies |

A month is counted only when the day of the month the account was opened has come round again, and the count never falls below one, so an account not yet a whole month old is spread over one month and the charge is taken at the level it was set. Equality satisfies each threshold.
